title: DASP: self-supervised nighttime monocular depth estimation with domain adaptation of spatiotemporal priors
core_idea: Introduce DASP, a self-supervised framework that improves monocular depth estimation at night by adapting daytime spatiotemporal priors via an adversarial branch and a self-supervised learning branch. The adversarial branch's discriminator uses spatiotemporal priors learning blocks (SPLB) combining a spatial-based temporal learning module (STLM) that applies orthogonal differencing to capture motion-related temporal variations and an axial spatial learning module (ASLM) that uses local asymmetric convolutions with global axial attention to capture multiscale structural information, enabling transfer of robust spatiotemporal features to nighttime depth estimation.
tldr: DASP leverages adversarial domain adaptation of learned daytime spatiotemporal priors (via STLM and ASLM) within a self-supervised framework to tackle low visibility and illumination variability in nighttime monocular depth estimation.
